title: Concurrent Sumatriptan Use and Gepant Overturn Authorizations
content:
Concurrent triptan treatment changes how the overturn ceiling of a gepant — Ubrelvy or Nurtec ODT — is worked out under the Utilization Management Program, acting on the drug's limit times the multiple as already worked out for concurrent opioid use (the result of the opioid step).

**Rule.**

- When the drug is a gepant and the member has paid sumatriptan retail fills **both in the last month and in the month before it**, the average monthly sumatriptan tablets over those two months divided by 2, the tablets of one triptan treatment, are subtracted.
- When the drug is a gepant and the member has paid sumatriptan fills in **exactly one** of those two months, the result is multiplied by 0.95.
- Otherwise, and always for a sumatriptan overturn, it is used as it stands.

The sumatriptan fills are paid retail claims under the Retail Pharmacy Network Benefit. The months end on the date the authorization is put in force: the last month is the fills dated after the same day of the month one month before that date, and the month before it is those dated within the last two months but not the last month. The average monthly tablets are the sumatriptan tablets of both months together divided by 2.

## Worked figures (hypothetical: Ubrelvy overturn, result of the opioid step 18)

| Sumatriptan tablets, last month | Sumatriptan tablets, month before | Treatment | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6 | 4 | 10 divided by 2 is 5 a month; 5 divided by 2 is 2.5, subtracted | 15.5 |
| 9 | 9 | 18 divided by 2 is 9; 9 divided by 2 is 4.5, subtracted | 13.5 |
| 6 | 0 | multiplied by 0.95 | 17.1 |
| 0 | 0 | as it stands | 18 |

For a sumatriptan overturn the figure stands whatever sumatriptan the member filled.
